findings.reason: as written a node reading §3's measure would treat the family as applyable once §12 lands, while the declared dependency (and reality) requires §14 first; the done-when's prerequisite range must be extended through §14 (and §13 for its log).
findings.text: §3's done-when states the family converges "after §5 to §12 have landed", but _document (line 23) now declares s3 depending on §13 and §14, and §14 is a hard prerequisite: the live apply is refused until the recommended-name guard stops protecting the merged PR #3, so §3 cannot meet its done-when without §14 (its own comment c-s3-lead-ruling-guard says "After §13 and §14 land, the boundary-averaged density family applies unforced").

findings.reason: the plan needs to say what protects a merged request whose fold-back has not landed (protect until approved, or record the lead's acceptance of the gap); the stated justification does not hold against its own evidence.
findings.text: §14 argues a merged request needs no roster protection because "a merged request protects through the fold-back it triggers, which sets name_stage=approved", yet the same section's own evidence is a merged request (catalog PR #3, merged 2026-09-01) whose fold-back never ran — the member still reads name_stage=accepted — so the compensating mechanism it invokes did not fire in the one case §14 and §3 act on, leaving catalog-published text that a physicist already reviewed with no protection at all, which is precisely what §3 (line 155, "or has already reviewed") says the guard exists to prevent.

findings.reason: the ten-rosters count for the member is correct and the one null-pr roster changes neither the guard's mechanism nor the done-when.
findings.text: §14 says the member "sits in the ten WEST task-2e rosters, which recorded fork pull requests 3 to 15", but of the ten rosters that name the member, `v0.3.0rc7+west-task-2e.sn_names.yaml` records `pr_number: null`, so only nine recorded a candidate request and only those nine contribute evidence (`protection.py:203` skips a roster with no pr_number/pr_url).

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited symbol resolves: `sn.py` harmonize 5909, `sn edit` 6849, `run_inline_review` call 7132, `sn rescore` 8357, `sn review` 6433, `sn run` 3031; `protection.py` `_frozen_roster_requests` 172 and `recommended_name_protections` 212; `promote.py` `parse_pull_request_url` 1448, `_pull_request_call` 1459, `_pull_request_state` 1557; `harmonize.py` `preview_recommended_refusals` 1382 and `refuse_recommended_members` 1412; extensionless hrefs are the house convention.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §13's structural and behavioural tests each name a removing-the-call control ("Each test fails with its call removed, recorded with EXIT="), and §14's four bullets each state "Each test fails with its mechanism removed"; each is a control that can redden.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — neither §13 nor §14 routes evidence to a scratchpad or node-local path; their gate logs land under the run and evidence directories the plan's other nodes already use.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach §13's or §14's new symbols; the stem token `sn-<command>` is a format, not a label (note: the existing `sn run` uses stem `sn`, so the stated stem rule is not what that command already does; the tests do not assert the stem for it).
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §14 justifies treating a merged request as non-protecting by asserting "a merged request protects through the fold-back it triggers, which sets name_stage=approved" (plan.html:249), a mechanism its own evidence in the same paragraph shows did not fire for exactly this case.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §13 carries one deliverable (every spending `sn` command writes a log) and §14 one (the guard protects only an open request); neither joins two separately-failing repairs.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §3's done-when still reserves the family apply for "after §5 to §12 have landed" (plan.html:182), while _document now declares s3 depending on §13 and §14 (plan.html:23), and §3's own recorded reasoning says the family cannot apply until §14 lands.
